newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin says prefers S&P's credit rating.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin says prefers S&P's credit rating.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin told reporters on Thursday he hoped the Dominion Bond Rating Service (DBRS) would better reflect the federal government's improved finances.

DBRS raised Canada's credit rating on Thursday to stable from negative because of progress on the fiscal front. But it said the long-term rating remained negative, citing high debt and the continuing separatist movement in Quebec.

"I think there was a mixed message from DBRS. I must say, I was quite happy with what Standard and Poor's did...and I would hope that the other rating agencies will recognize along with DBRS the improving situation in Canada," Martin said.
Standard and Poor's on February 24 upgraded Canada's foreign currency credit rating to stable from negative but said high debt prevented a full rating upgrade.

Asked if Quebec uncertainty was currently a major factor, Martin said: "No, I don't. I certaintly understand that political uncertainty is a major obstacle to any country or in fact any province's credit rating."
